headline: Midasu is from 乱れる (midareru, “to be confused, to be disordered”).
Sanjō appears to be a Japanese coinage, 参 (san, “to come, to go”, humble connotations) plus 上 (jō, “up, upwards”).
Chūgaeri is 宙 (chū, “mid-air”) plus 返り (kaeri), the stem of 返る (kaeru).
パンク covers “puncture” and “punk”, and the source takes both from English.
Shuju is a reduplication of 種 (shu, “type; kind”), with shu voiced to ju by rendaku.
Heijō is from Middle Chinese 平常 and first appears in the 818 CE compilation 文華秀麗集 (Bunka Shūrei Shū).
レベル is from English level.
グレー is from English grey or gray.
Yugamu is from Old Japanese, possibly related to 弓 (yumi, “bow”).
Ii-kagen is いい (ii, “good”) plus 加減 (kagen, “amount”), a shift from earlier よい加減 (yoikagen), attested from the 18th century.
Shitsuke is a nominalization of 仕付け (shitsuke, literally “training”), the stem of 仕付ける (shitsukeru).
ホース is from Dutch hoos.
Ore was originally a second person pronoun, as used in the Kojiki of 712 CE, and gradually became a first person pronoun.
レンタカー is from English rent-a-car.
Chōshinki is 聴診 (chōshin, “auscultation”) plus 器 (-ki, “instrument, device”).
Nemutai is compared with 眠る (nemuru, “to sleep”), 眠い (nemui, “sleepy”) and おねむ (o-nemu), all related to Classical Japanese 寝 (nu, “to sleep”).
Haigūsha is, by surface analysis, 配偶 (haigū) plus 者 (-sha).
Higoro is 日 (hi, “day”) plus 頃 (koro, “(approximate) time”), with koro voiced to goro by rendaku.
In hojo, 補 is a daiyōji replacing 輔.
Ton'ya is a shift from toiya.
サイクル is from English cycle.
タイピスト is from English typist.
Kasei is from Middle Chinese 火星, literally “fire star”.
カルテ is borrowed from German Karte, and is a doublet of カルタ (karuta) and カード (kādo).
エアメール is borrowed from English airmail.
In shinryaku, 略 is a daiyōji replacing 掠.
Ketsu, “decision”, is from Middle Chinese 決 (MC kwet).
カット is from English cut.
Kura is related to 黒 (kuro, “black”).
Atai is possibly the conjunctive form of the verb 能う (atau).
Muron is from Middle Chinese 無論, literally “without discussion, no argument”.
